grades.reason: Only describes a shell pipeline (`ls | say`) as an example of a pipe between two programs. It says nothing about EOF, closing write ends, or child termination.

grades.quote: The exit system call causes the calling process to stop executing and to release resources such as memory and open files.
grades.reason: Covers fork, exit and wait. It says exit releases the process's open files, which is the only link to a child's pipe end being closed. It never mentions pipes or EOF, and it doesn't say the parent's copy of the write end must also be closed.

grades.quote: piperead() { acquire(&pipe->lock); while(no data in pipe->buffer) { Holding pipe->lock sleep(&pipe, &pipe->lock)
grades.reason: Figure fragment showing piperead sleeping while the pipe buffer has no data. This matches the symptom of a reader that blocks. It says nothing about EOF or write-end closure.

grades.quote: A reference count tracks the number of references to a particular open file.
grades.reason: Explains that open files, including pipes, are reference-counted. Fork and dup can share one open file across processes, and the underlying pipe is released only when the count reaches zero. This hints at why a write end held by another process, such as the parent, would keep a pipe from ending. It never says EOF depends on all write ends being closed.
